title: Rumour: LEGO SMART Play could get a small 81-piece 'All-in-one Activator' in 2027
summary: An unconfirmed leak points to a new low-piece-count SMART Play All-in-one set, numbered 72118, said to arrive next April. Take it as a rumour for now.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A rumour circulating via leak account Buggyleaks, and shared through carter_bricks04's Instagram Story, suggests LEGO SMART Play could see a new All-in-one set called 72118 All-in-one Activator launch in April 2027. Unusually, it's said to contain just 81 pieces — far fewer than any All-in-one SMART Play set released so far.

All-in-one SMART Play sets currently bundle everything needed to use the system: a SMART Brick, wireless charger, SMART Tags, and sometimes a SMART Minifigure. The five All-in-one sets available today are all Star Wars or Pokémon themed, with the smallest being 72164 Training House at 400 pieces for £59.99.

No price or theme has been mentioned for 72118. Given the much smaller piece count, a lower price than existing All-in-one sets seems likely, though that's speculation at this stage. SMART Play itself is rumoured to expand into Star Wars, NINJAGO and Disney themes in 2027, but this particular set isn't tied to any of those in the current leak.

**This is unofficial and unconfirmed.** LEGO Group has not announced this set, and details should be treated cautiously until confirmed.

## Why it matters
SMART Play is still a young system, and any move towards a cheaper, smaller entry point could make it more accessible for new fans or as an add-on for existing collections. If accurate, an 81-piece All-in-one could signal LEGO testing lower price tiers for the format — useful context for anyone tracking where this product line is headed.

## What to watch next
Watch for further leaks or an official reveal confirming (or denying) 72118, its theme, and pricing. As always with early rumours, details could change significantly before release.

title: LEGO Ideas: how The X-Files alien minifigure was designed for safety and silliness
summary: LEGO designers have revealed the thinking behind the new grey alien minifigure in LEGO Ideas 21369 The X-Files, including a safety-driven design choice that doubles as a fun feature.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Ideas 21369 The X-Files is now out, and LEGO Group designers have shared behind-the-scenes details on how the set's grey alien minifigure head came together. According to Element Designer Nicola Belfiore and Model Design Master Chris McVeigh, the team wanted the alien to nod to the classic '90s-style depiction of extraterrestrials, with a bulbous grey head that still felt in proportion to a standard minifigure.

Getting the size right took some trial and error - a straight scaled-down version looked like a shrunken alien head, so the designers deliberately made it slightly oversized to match reference material.

Once the shape was locked in, LEGO's product safety team stepped in. They found the small head element carried a choking risk, so a hole was added to the top to allow airflow if swallowed. The designers turned that requirement into a feature by making the hole a standard 1.5 minifigure accessory connector - meaning fans can now pop hats, sunglasses, or a tiara onto the alien's head.

## Why it matters
This is a good example of how LEGO safety requirements and creative design work together rather than against each other. For collectors and builders, it's also a nice reminder that small design choices - like an accessory socket - can add extra display and customisation value to a single minifigure.

## What to watch next
Fans of LEGO Ideas sets may want to keep an eye out for further behind-the-scenes documentaries or design commentary from the LEGO Group on upcoming licensed builds.

title: Eagle-eyed fans spot LEGO Star Wars mix-up in new Spider-Man film

Adding to the fun, Brick Fanatics notes the film is set in 2028 - by which point both real-world sets would already have retired.

**Note:** the mix-up theory is Brick Fanatics' own analysis based on close inspection of screen stills, not a confirmed statement from the film's production team.

## Why it matters
It's a lighthearted reminder of how closely LEGO fans scrutinise set appearances in film and TV - and how easy it is for prop departments to slip up when handling real, retired sets. For collectors, it's also a nice spot-the-difference exercise between two similar X-Wing builds from different eras.

Waller, who has used the username 'Wetwired' across LEGO Ideas and other platforms for years, said he was keen to see the reference included once the connection became clear. He also noted a possible secondary link between the tapes and the show's Mulder character, though he said this wasn't something the team had deliberately planned.

title: LEGO releases behind-the-scenes documentary for The X-Files Ideas set
summary: A new official LEGO documentary explores the design of 21369 The X-Files, focusing on the tricky triangular UFO build.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has released an official documentary-style video covering the design of the recently launched LEGO Ideas set 21369 The X-Files. Published on LEGO.com as part of the ongoing 'Secrets of our Sets' series (which appears to be replacing the older LEGO Designer Videos format), it follows a similar release for 11377 The Lord of the Rings: Minas Tirith.

The video digs into the challenges of recreating the set's UFO element, which designer Chris McVeigh describes as a genuinely tough build due to its perfect triangular shape - something LEGO elements aren't typically suited to. To solve it, the team reused a technique involving the golden ring element as a spacer to lock the sides to the centre, previously used on 10289 Bird of Paradise.

The documentary also explains why the UFO doesn't spin, despite that seeming like an obvious play feature. Designers say this was a deliberate choice for accuracy to the show, since that craft type doesn't rotate in flight, and adding a spin mechanism would have required cross-axles and gears that would compromise the set's transparent display stand.

## Why it matters
For fans and collectors, these documentaries offer a rare look at the real design decisions and building techniques behind official LEGO Ideas sets, which can be genuinely useful inspiration for custom builders and MOC creators tackling awkward geometric shapes.

## What to watch next
Watch for whether LEGO continues rolling out 'Secrets of our Sets' documentaries as a regular feature for future Ideas and Icons releases.

title: LEGO Architecture designer explains how new Tower Bridge set ups the realism
summary: The designer behind LEGO Architecture's new 21067 Tower Bridge has explained how the model builds on the 2010 Creator Expert version, with added realism and a lighter, easier-to-display build.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Senior Model Designer Jae Won has spoken to LEGO.com about designing 21067 Tower Bridge, the new 3,745-piece LEGO Architecture set that recently launched as a spiritual successor to 2010's 10214 Tower Bridge from the Creator Expert range.

Jae, a former architect, revealed he travelled to London to take reference photos of the real bridge during early development, a trip he described as confidential even from his own family at the time.

According to Jae, the standout addition in the new set is a model of the river beneath the bridge, something the original 2010 version lacked. He also said the team "dialled up the overall level of realism" in the architectural details, with the new set - despite being built to a smaller scale than its predecessor - featuring proportions and details closer to the real landmark. The set has also been engineered to be lighter and easier to move for display purposes.
